source_items.title: Entrance Object: Strait as chokepoint
source_items.text: Object frame: begin with the Strait of Hormuz as a strategic object rather than a headline event. The point is to let the operator see geography, recognition, transit, and restraint as one object cluster before moving to policy options.

source_items.title: Object Sequence: Recognition, transit, restraint
source_items.text: Interpretive sequence: recognition decides who is seen as escalatory, transit decides who feels immediate cost, and restraint decides whether pressure remains coercive or becomes a legitimacy loss. This object sequence is meant to be walked, not skimmed.

source_items.title: Operational Relevance: Counterweights and decision points
source_items.text: Operator use: the exhibit lane should end by naming counterweights, shipping exposure, recognition traps, and off-ramps. The deck should help an operator brief the object without collapsing it into one forecast.

source_items.title: Caution Object: What this deck is not
source_items.text: Caution: this is an exhibit-style strategy deck, not canonical Record, not a legal memo, and not a direct prediction engine. Its job is to clarify the object sequence and improve briefing depth.
